title: Church singing and learning piano chords from a friend
summary: Church on Liberty and St. Peter, preachers and choirs, singing at school and house parties; a young piano friend showed him chords and Indian Love Call.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well that cooperators is a church now, right? Yeah. Did you hear any good church music when you were a kid? Oh yeah. Did you belong to any church?

Yeah, I was christened Catholic but my mother was Baptist and we used to go to a church that's not far from the cooperators hall, it was on Liberty and St. Peter. And it was, the pastor's name was Ella Cole.
It's still there. I think you're going to tear that place down now. It's still there? I think maybe there's one out there on St. Peter.

St. Peter and Liberty, yeah. The auditorium. That's right. And at that time, we used to call it Ella Cole's Church. And oh, they had some wonderful singing. I heard preachers like Blind Frank, which was one of the greatest preachers they had in New Orleans as I knew of at that time. But I used to have all these choirs, I used to love that. I used to love to go to church and hear this singing. I didn't know much about the church but I loved the singing, you know? But what really inspired me to play music, I was, I went to school and in school I mean, I used to sing. And I had a pretty good voice, you know? And later years I had a lot of piano players like Lil Willie, Georgie, Parker, Red Caillou and all those fellas. And I used to sing with them at house parties. And then I met this little guy who became a wonderful friend of mine, this little boy in San Diego, who was a marvelous piano player. And I began to go around with him singing at different parties and different things, bumming around with him. So I used to like to sing so much that he showed me some chords on the piano. He wasn't a reader but he could play a lot of piano. What type of piano did he play?
He wasn't just a blues man. He played any type of piano.

He played classic, regs, popular, anything he heard he played and he played it very well. Anybody in New Orleans will tell you that. That's right. He was one of the greatest piano players. He began to show me a few little chords on the piano and then when I wasn't with him I'd go around some balls that had a piano in practice. Well I learned how to play Stagger Lee and different other blues you know that they played down there. And I met a fellow one time at a ballroom who taught me how to play Indian Love Call. That was the first popular number I learned how to play. And I learned how to play it in C, which is written in E flat. But I always not, still play it in C when I play. And that started me, fooling around with the piano.
